⏺ The problem is widespread — the agents invented an entirely new persistent-SSE
  model and wrote it into Part 11. The actual design is one new SSE connection 
  per turn: client POSTs a message, opens a fresh GET /chat/stream, the server
  streams and closes. sourceMessageState: "COMPLETED" is the turn-end signal. No
  turn_complete, no session_close.

⏺ Final check — no turn_complete or session_close remaining anywhere:

  Searched for 1 pattern (ctrl+o to expand)

⏺ Clean. All references removed.

  The agents hallucinated a persistent-SSE model because they pattern-matched on
  WebSocket-style "keep the connection open" thinking. The actual design is
  simpler and more robust: one new SSE per turn. This is the same model OpenAI,
  Anthropic, and every major LLM API uses — stateless HTTP, no long-lived socket
  to manage, works through any proxy or CDN, any backend node handles any turn.

  The sourceMessageState: "COMPLETED" on the final chat_event is all the FE
  needs to know the turn is done. The HTTP response just closes.

⏺ Clean. Here's what changed and why:

  Removed everywhere: auth_required SSE event type — it never existed in the
  plan.

  The two auth patterns now correctly documented:

  1. FE-handled (shortlist_property, contact_seller): These FE templates handle
  login internally. requires_auth=False on the IntentRecord. No BE auth check
  needed — the FE is responsible.
  2. BE-data-gated (portfolio/saved_properties, portfolio/viewed_properties,
  portfolio/recent_searches, portfolio/recommendations,
  property_search/save_alert): requires_auth=True. When auth_token is absent,
  route_node sets bot_response to build_login_template_response(...), and
  emit_final_state emits:
    - chat_event { seq:0, text: "Log in to see your saved properties.", 
  IN_PROGRESS }
    - chat_event { seq:1, templateId: "login", data: {}, COMPLETED }

  The login template is now in the template inventory in api-contract.md Part
  D8, and the emit_final_state in solid-architecture.md handles the combined
  text+template case.

  Session State Tracker

  search_history:     []

  ---
  Turn 1 — "show me 2bhk properties in powai"

  Request Reception (FastAPI)

  POST /chat/message
  Headers: session-token: sess_x9k2m
  Body: { "content": "show me 2bhk properties in powai", "conversationId":
  "conv_abc123" }

  Handler validates session_token against gateway. Creates request_id: req_001.
  Opens BotState with make_base_state().

  ---
  SLM Classification (classify_node)

  What the SLM receives:

  [SYSTEM — Section 1: Identity + Domain Guard]
  You are a real estate intent classifier for Housing.com India.
  Output strict JSON only. No prose.

  [SECTION 2: Intent Taxonomy]
  (auto-generated from INTENT_REGISTRY — ~2,500 tokens covering all intents)
  ...
  property_search / filter_search: User wants to search properties with filters.
    filter_delta keys: bhk (array), localities (array), city, price_min,
  price_max,
    transaction_type (buy|rent), furnishing, carpet_area_min/max, amenities...
  ...

  [SECTION 3: Filter Delta Rules]
  (auto-generated from FILTER_REGISTRY — ADD vs REPLACE semantics, inference
  rules)
  ...
  BHK: REPLACE on explicit list. "3bhk" → {bhk:[3]}. "3 and 4bhk" → {bhk:[3,4]}.
  price: infer transaction_type from scale. "1.5cr" → buy, price_max:15000000.
  locality: always REPLACE unless "also", "as well", "and" → ADD.
  ...

  [SECTION 4: Conversation History]

✻ Brewed for 5m 58s

❯ in Turn 6 if instead of typing "show me properties in 2nd and 3rd localities  
  from this" user had typed "i like Kanjurmarg and Mulund. show me properties"  
  or had typed "mujhe doosri aur teesri localities pasand hai, inme property    
  dikhao" or had typed "i like 2, 3 number localities, show properties here".   
  what would have happened in each case?                                        

⏺ Three very different resolution paths. Let me trace each.

  ---
  Case A — "i like Kanjurmarg and Mulund. show me properties"

  What changes: no ordinal resolver, direct entity resolution

  The pre-pass ordinal resolver in resolve_entities_node sees no positional
  language. The SLM receives the raw message.

  SLM output:
  {
    "main_intent": "property_search",
    "sub_intent":  "filter_search",
    "entities_mentioned": [
      { "name": "Kanjurmarg", "inferred_type": "locality" },
      { "name": "Mulund",     "inferred_type": "locality" }
    ],
    "pivot":        true,
    "filter_delta": {
      "localities": ["Kanjurmarg", "Mulund"]
    },
    "clarification_needed": null,
    "reasoning": "Explicit locality names. Pivot from locality_research back to 
  property_search."
  }

  The ambiguity problem — resolve_entities_node

  Neither name is unambiguous. Autosuggest returns:

  resolveEntity("Kanjurmarg", type="locality", city="Mumbai", service="buy")
  → candidates:
      { uuid: "loc_kan_w", display_name: "Kanjurmarg West",  score: 0.87 }
      { uuid: "loc_kan_e", display_name: "Kanjurmarg East",  score: 0.84 }

  resolveEntity("Mulund", type="locality", city="Mumbai", service="buy")
  → candidates:
      { uuid: "loc_mul_w", display_name: "Mulund West",  score: 0.88 }
      { uuid: "loc_mul_e", display_name: "Mulund East",  score: 0.82 }

  Both have 2 candidates with close scores. Without context this triggers
  clarification. But — Turn 5's carousel is in session history. The resolver
  applies a prior context confidence boost: if a candidate appeared in the
  immediately preceding carousel, its score gets a +0.15 boost.

  Kanjurmarg West appeared in Turn 5 carousel at position 2 → score: 0.87 + 0.15
  = 1.02 → winner
  Mulund West appeared in Turn 5 carousel at position 3    → score: 0.88 + 0.15
  = 1.03 → winner

  Both resolve cleanly. No clarification_needed. Pipeline continues identically
  to the original Turn 6.

  Key difference from ordinal path: The ordinal resolver is a pure lookup
  (carousel_state[2] and carousel_state[3]) — O(1), no API call, confidence 1.0.
  This path calls autosuggest twice (~50ms each) and relies on the context
  boost working correctly. If the user had typed "Kanjurmarg" when Turn 5 had
  shown "Kanjurmarg East" instead of "Kanjurmarg West", the boost would amplify
  the wrong answer.

  What user sees: Identical result. Marginally slower (~100ms autosuggest
  overhead vs ~0ms ordinal lookup).

  ---
  Case B — "mujhe doosri aur teesri localities pasand hai, inme property dikhao"

  What changes: multilingual pipeline

  normalize_node runs first. Its job is lightweight normalization — trim,
  deduplicate whitespace, detect script. It does not translate. Claude Haiku
  handles the Hindi natively.

  SLM classification (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 is multilingual):

  The SLM reads the Hindi directly. "Doosri" = second, "teesri" = third. It
  understands the ordinal intent.

  {
    "main_intent": "property_search",
    "sub_intent":  "filter_search",
    "entities_mentioned": [],
    "pivot":        true,
    "filter_delta": {
      "localities": ["__ordinal_2__", "__ordinal_3__"]
    },
    "clarification_needed": null,
    "reasoning": "Hindi: 'doosri' = 2nd, 'teesri' = 3rd. Positional references 
  to prior locality carousel. 'inme' = 'in these'."
  }

  The SLM uses an __ordinal_N__ sentinel (defined in the SLM prompt taxonomy
  section) to signal positional references that the orchestrator must resolve.

  The multilingual ordinal problem — resolve_entities_node

  The pre-pass ordinal resolver must recognise "doosri" and "teesri" as
  ordinals. If the ordinal table only covers English:

  ORDINAL_WORDS = {
    'first': 1, '1st': 1, 'second': 2, '2nd': 2, 'third': 3, '3rd': 3, ...
  }

  Hindi ordinals are not in this table. Two outcomes depending on
  implementation:

  ---
  Outcome B1 — Ordinal resolver handles multilingual (correct implementation)

  The SLM already resolved the semantic meaning (outputting __ordinal_2__ and
  __ordinal_3__ in filter_delta). The orchestrator's ordinal resolver just looks
  up carousel_state[2] and carousel_state[3] from Turn 5:

  carousel_state[2] → { locality_id: "loc_kan_w", display_name: "Kanjurmarg
  West" }
  carousel_state[3] → { locality_id: "loc_mul_w", display_name: "Mulund West" }

  Resolves identically to the original. The SLM did the heavy lifting — it
  translated the semantic ordinal into a machine-readable sentinel. The resolver
  just does the lookup.

  User experience: Identical result. Hindi works seamlessly.

  ---
  Outcome B2 — SLM doesn't emit sentinels, outputs raw Hindi ordinals (gap)

  If the SLM instead outputs:
  {
    "filter_delta": { "localities": ["doosri locality", "teesri locality"] }
  }

  The resolve_entities_node autosuggest call for "doosri locality" returns zero
  results. The resolver logs a slm_malformed_entities warning. The entity drops
  out.

  clarify_node detects localities is now empty but city and service are present.
  Emits:

  chat_event { templateId: "nested_qna",
    data: { selections: [{
      questionId: "q_locality",
      title: "Which localities would you like to explore?",
      type: "text_input"
    }]}
  }

  Recovery path: User types "Kanjurmarg West and Mulund West" → Case A flow. One
  extra round-trip.

  ---
  What this exposes about the architecture

  The SLM prompt taxonomy section (auto-generated from INTENT_REGISTRY) is in
  English. The SLM is instructed to output JSON in English with specific field
  names and sentinel values regardless of the input language. When the SLM is
  multilingual-capable and the prompt is clear about sentinel format, Outcome B1
  is achieved. This should be validated in the evaluation suite with
  multilingual test cases — currently the taxonomy checklist only requires
  adding examples in slm/examples/<intent>.md, and those examples are likely
  English-only.

  Action item this surfaces: The evaluation framework in
  slm-classifier-design.md needs multilingual examples (Hindi, Hinglish, Tamil,
  etc.) to guarantee Outcome B1.

  ---
  Case C — "i like 2, 3 number localities, show properties here"

  What changes: ambiguous numeric phrasing

  This is Indian English — "2, 3 number" is a regional construction meaning
  "numbers 2 and 3" (position markers). The SLM needs to interpret whether "2,
  3" are:
  - Ordinal positions in the carousel (correct interpretation)
  - BHK configuration (wrong — would be "2, 3 BHK")
  - The number of localities (wrong — "2-3 localities")

  SLM classification:

  The SLM uses conversation context (prior turn = locality carousel) to resolve
  the ambiguity. "2, 3 number localities" + context of a just-shown locality
  list → positional references.

  {
    "main_intent": "property_search",
    "sub_intent":  "filter_search",
    "entities_mentioned": [],
    "pivot":        true,
    "filter_delta": {
      "localities": ["__ordinal_2__", "__ordinal_3__"]
    },
    "clarification_needed": null,
    "reasoning": "'2, 3 number localities' = positional refs. Prior turn showed 
  locality carousel. Not BHK (no BHK context). Resolves to 2nd and 3rd carousel 
  entries."
  }

  Same sentinel output as Case B. Same resolution path. Works identically.

  But what if the SLM gets it wrong?

  The critical ambiguity is with BHK. If the user had said "show me 2, 3 number
  properties" instead of "localities", the SLM might have output filter_delta: {
  bhk: [2, 3] } instead of ordinal positions. The word "localities" is the
  disambiguating signal here — it ties "2, 3 number" to the locality carousel,
  not to BHK.

  If "localities" were absent — e.g., "i like 2, 3, show properties" — the SLM
  would be in genuine ambiguity territory and should output:

  {
    "clarification_needed": "Did you mean 2 and 3 BHK properties, or the 2nd and
  3rd localities shown above?",
    "reasoning": "Ambiguous: '2, 3' could be BHK or ordinal positions. Need 
  confirmation."
  }

  clarify_node fires, nested_qna emitted:
  "Did you mean 2 and 3 BHK properties, or the 2nd and 3rd localities shown
  above?"
    Options: [{ id: "bhk", title: "2 & 3 BHK types" },
              { id: "ordinal", title: "2nd & 3rd localities" }]

  ---
  Side-by-Side: What Actually Differs

  SLM burden
  Original ("2nd and 3rd localities"): Low — ordinal is unambiguous
  Case A (explicit names): Low — entity names explicit
  Case B (Hindi): Medium — multilingual ordinals
  Case C (numeric): Medium — numeric ambiguity resolved by context
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Ordinal resolver
  Original ("2nd and 3rd localities"): Direct carousel_state[N] lookup
  Case A (explicit names): Not used
  Case B (Hindi): Used (via SLM sentinel)
  Case C (numeric): Used (via SLM sentinel)
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Entity resolution
  Original ("2nd and 3rd localities"): No autosuggest call
  Case A (explicit names): 2 autosuggest calls + context boost
  Case B (Hindi): No autosuggest call
  Case C (numeric): No autosuggest call
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Clarification risk
  Original ("2nd and 3rd localities"): None
  Case A (explicit names): Low (context boost usually wins)
  Case B (Hindi): None (if SLM emits sentinels correctly)
  Case C (numeric): Low (word "localities" disambiguates)
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Latency delta
  Original ("2nd and 3rd localities"): Baseline
  Case A (explicit names): +~100ms (2 autosuggest calls)
  Case B (Hindi): Same as baseline
  Case C (numeric): Same as baseline
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Multilingual gap
  Original ("2nd and 3rd localities"): n/a
  Case A (explicit names): n/a
  Case B (Hindi): Exposes Hindi ordinal eval gap
  Case C (numeric): n/a
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Result
  Original ("2nd and 3rd localities"): Kanjurmarg W + Mulund W
  Case A (explicit names): Kanjurmarg W + Mulund W
  Case B (Hindi): Kanjurmarg W + Mulund W
  Case C (numeric): Kanjurmarg W + Mulund W

  The architecture is designed such that all four phrasings land at the same
  answer. The ordinal path (original, Cases B and C) is fastest and most
  reliable because it bypasses autosuggest entirely. The explicit-name path
  (Case A) is nearly as reliable but adds latency and has a non-zero
  disambiguation risk if the prior carousel context boost logic has a bug.

⏺ Good question to pause on. My opinion: don't lazy-load, but do tier the filter
  vocabulary within the prompt. Here's the full reasoning across each
  dimension.

  ---
  The list_tools / lazy-load pattern is wrong for this specific case

  The key insight is that the SLM is doing discriminated classification, not
  open-ended tool selection. These are fundamentally different tasks.

  For an LLM doing open-ended reasoning (Sonnet planning a multi-step task),
  lazy tool discovery makes sense — it doesn't need to know about getFloorPlans
  while deciding whether to call searchProperties.

  For a structured JSON classifier that must pick exactly one (main_intent, 
  sub_intent) tuple from a finite set, the taxonomy is not a menu to browse —
  it's the output schema. The model needs to see all valid outputs to make a
  discriminated choice. Hiding locality_research/trending_localities from the
  upfront prompt doesn't save tokens — it causes the SLM to force-fit "show me
  trending areas" into property_search/filter_search, which is a
  misclassification.

  ---
  Cost reality check — the numbers don't justify it

  Full taxonomy, cached:   ~2,500 tokens × 10% cache cost = 250 effective
  tokens/call
  Truncated taxonomy:      ~600 tokens (uncached for primary-only)
  Saving per call:         ~150 tokens = ~$0.00012/call at Haiku pricing

  At 1M calls/day: saving = $120/day

  That's real money at scale, but the prompt cache is already doing 90% of this
  work for free. The real question is whether $120/day justifies the
  architectural complexity, quality risk, and engineering cost of building and
  maintaining a two-stage classification pipeline.

  It doesn't.

  ---
  The hallucination concern is actually inverted

  More taxonomy tokens → less hallucination for a classifier. The taxonomy
  constrains the output space. When the SLM sees that property_type has exactly
  [apartment, builder_floor, plot, villa, independent_house], it can't invent
  "studio" or "penthouse". When it's not shown those options, it fills from
  training priors — which is where hallucination comes from.

  The concern is valid if the SLM were generating prose. For constrained JSON
  output, a richer schema is a guardrail, not a liability.

  ---
  What IS worth doing — tiering within the prompt, not excluding from it

  Your instinct about primary vs. secondary is right, just applied at the wrong
  level. Don't split into two calls. Split within the single prompt:

  FILTER DELTA — PRIMARY (covers ~85% of queries):
    bhk:                  [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
    price_min/max:        integer (rupees)
    property_type:        [apartment, builder_floor, plot, villa,
  independent_house]
    listed_by:            [owner, broker]
    construction_status:  [ready_to_move, under_construction]
    amenities:            [lift, gym, swimming_pool, gated_community, parking,
  gas_pipeline]
    localities:           [array of names — resolve_entities handles IDs]
    transaction_type:     [buy, rent]

  FILTER DELTA — EXTENDED (emit only when explicitly stated by user):
    furnishing:           [furnished, semi_furnished, unfurnished]
    sale_type:            [new_booking, resale]
    carpet_area_min/max:  integer (sqft)
    facing:               [east, west, north, south]
    floor_min/max:        integer
    is_verified:          boolean
    has_photos:           boolean
    age_years_max:        integer
    (... 15+ more)

  Same for intents — primary block with full descriptions, secondary block with
  one-line terse descriptions:

  PRIMARY INTENTS (full description + examples):
    property_search/filter_search
    property_detail/property_about
    portfolio/recent_searches
    locality_research/trending_localities
    property_detail/similar_properties

  SECONDARY INTENTS (terse — one line each):
    locality_research/commute_time: "User asks commute time from a locality to a
  destination"
    locality_research/price_trends: "Price appreciation in a locality over time"
    comparison/compare_localities:  "Side-by-side comparison of two named
  localities"
    ... (etc.)

  This achieves:
  - SLM learns to prefer primary options → fewer filter hallucinations
  - SLM still sees full output space → no misclassification at intent boundaries
  - Token count drops modestly (~30-40%) → smaller cache miss cost
  - Zero new failure modes, zero added latency, zero pipeline complexity

  ---
  The scaling concern — valid, but the solution is registry hygiene not lazy 
  loading

  As intents grow:
  1. The auto-generator enforces structure (descriptions stay terse for
  secondary intents)
  2. You set a hard token budget for the taxonomy block (say 3,000 tokens) and
  the generator enforces it — if it overflows, it compresses secondary intent
  descriptions first
  3. Intents that are never fired in production (check via slm_classification
  metric grouped by intent) get pruned from the registry entirely

  The list_tools approach pushes the complexity into the runtime path. Registry
  hygiene pushes it into the development workflow. The latter is much cheaper to
  maintain.

  ---
  Summary verdict

  ┌────────────┬─────────────┬──────────┬────────────────────┬────────────┐
  │  Approach  │ Performance │   Cost   │      Quality       │ Complexity │
  ├────────────┼─────────────┼──────────┼────────────────────┼────────────┤
  │ Current    │             │ Good     │                    │            │
  │ (full      │ Good        │ (cache   │ Good               │ Low        │
  │ upfront,   │             │ does the │                    │            │
  │ cached)    │             │  work)   │                    │            │
  ├────────────┼─────────────┼──────────┼────────────────────┼────────────┤
  │ Lazy load  │ Bad for 20% │          │ Worse              │            │
  │ /          │  of users   │ Marginal │ (misclassification │ High       │
  │ list_tools │ (2x         │  saving  │  risk)             │            │
  │            │ latency)    │          │                    │            │
  ├────────────┼─────────────┼──────────┼────────────────────┼────────────┤
  │ Tier       │             │          │ Better (guided     │            │
  │ within     │ Same        │ Slightly │ primary            │ Same       │
  │ single     │             │  better  │ preference)        │            │
  │ prompt     │             │          │                    │            │
  └────────────┴─────────────┴──────────┴────────────────────┴────────────┘

  Do the tiering. Skip the lazy loading. The list_tools pattern solves a real
  problem — just not this one.

⏺ Let me actually engage with each counter-argument seriously rather than defend
  my prior position.

  ---
  Point 1 — $120/day cost. You're right, I was too dismissive.

  My original estimate was lazy. Let me redo it honestly.

  At Housing.com's actual traffic scale — say 10M classification calls/day:

  Current full taxonomy (cached, 2,500 tokens):
    Cache reads: 10M × 2,500 × $0.08/1M = $2,000/day

  Tiered prompt (primary only, ~600 tokens):
    Cache reads: 10M × 600 × $0.08/1M = $480/day

  Saving: ~$1,520/day → ~$550K/year

  That's real money. I concede this point. Cost is a legitimate driver at this
  scale, not just a footnote.

  ---
  Point 2 — "Don't guess, load more tools." My real objection.

  Your instinct is sound in principle. My concern isn't philosophical — it's a
  specific failure mode of the implementation.

  You're proposing something like:

  "Here are the PRIMARY intents. If the user's message doesn't clearly
  fit these, output: { needs_more_context: true, domain_hint: "locality" }
  and I will provide more tools. Never guess."

  The problem is: Haiku's meta-uncertainty is unreliable. You're asking the
  model to correctly identify the boundary of its own knowledge — to know what
  it doesn't know. This is calibrated uncertainty, and smaller/faster models are
  notoriously bad at it.

  Consider this user message: "show me properties near good schools in Powai"

  With only the primary taxonomy visible:
  - Option A: Haiku confidently classifies → property_search/filter_search with
  amenities: [schools_nearby] ← correct
  - Option B: Haiku triggers needs_more_context because "good schools" feels
  like locality research ← wrong trigger
  - Option C: Haiku invents filter_delta: { nearby_schools: true } which doesn't
  exist in the schema ← hallucination

  In testing you'll tune examples to reduce B and C. But you'll never eliminate
  them. Every false positive on needs_more_context costs you one extra SLM
  round-trip — for a PRIMARY intent user. The very 85% you were trying to not
  pay extra for.

  The false positive rate matters more than the false negative rate here. A
  false negative (missing a secondary intent, routing to out_of_scope) is
  recoverable — user rephrases. A false positive (unnecessary list_tools on a
  primary intent) silently degrades p95 latency for your most common users.

  I'm not saying this approach is wrong. I'm saying it requires its own
  evaluation suite to tune the threshold, and that work is non-trivial.

  ---
  Point 3 — Terse secondary descriptions hurt quality. You're right, I was 
  hand-wavy.

  My one-liner approach was intellectually dishonest. Let me be concrete about
  what breaks.

  If locality_research/commute_time is described as just "commute time from 
  locality to destination", the SLM misses:

  - That filter_delta is empty for this intent (it's entity-driven, not
  filter-driven)
  - That it needs two entities: origin_locality and destination (not just one)
  - That it disambiguates from property_search when user says "how long from
  Powai to BKC" vs "properties near BKC"

  The terse description doesn't convey the discriminating signals. The model
  falls back to training priors to fill the gaps — which is exactly the
  hallucination vector I said the full taxonomy prevents.

  I was wrong to suggest terse descriptions solve the token problem cleanly.
  They don't.

  ---
  Point 4 — Dev hygiene. We agree it's a wash.

  Neither approach fixes this. Moving on.

  ---
  What This Means Re-evaluated Honestly

  So where does that leave us? Both of our initial positions have genuine
  problems:

  - Full taxonomy upfront: Real cost at scale, scaling ceiling as product grows
  - Lazy load with list_tools: False positive latency tax on primary users,
  Haiku meta-uncertainty unreliability
  - Terse secondary descriptions: Hurts quality for secondary intents

  Neither is right. Let me propose what I actually think the architecture should
  be, having thought harder.

  ---
  The Real Long-Term Answer — Hierarchical Cascade

  This is how large-scale NLU systems actually work at Google, Amazon, and
  similar. Not monolithic classifiers that grow forever, not lazy loading, but a
  two-stage cascade:

  Stage 1: Domain Router (tiny, fast)
    Input:  ~200 tokens (5 domain descriptions + current message)
    Output: domain ∈ { property_search | locality_research |
                       project_research | portfolio | financial | unclear }
    Latency: ~30ms (tiny prompt, fast output)
    Cost:   trivial

  Stage 2: Domain Classifier (full depth)
    Input:  Full taxonomy for the detected domain only (~500-800 tokens per
  domain)
    Output: (main_intent, sub_intent, filter_delta, entities, clarification)
    Latency: ~100ms
    Cost:   domain-scoped, not full-registry cost

  Why this is better than list_tools:

  Domain routing is a 5-way classification, not an open question about what the
  model doesn't know. Haiku is excellent at 5-way classification — it's a
  confident, bounded decision. No meta-uncertainty required.

  Why this is better than full taxonomy upfront:

  Each domain taxonomy stays small forever. Adding 10 new locality_research
  sub-intents doesn't bloat property_search classification. Domains are
  independently deployable — you can retrain the locality router without
  touching property search.

  Why this is better than terse secondary descriptions:

  Each domain classifier has full, rich descriptions for every intent in its
  domain. Quality is not compromised.

  The cost math:

  Stage 1: 200 tokens × $0.08/1M = $0.000016/call
  Stage 2: 700 tokens × $0.08/1M = $0.000056/call
  Total:   $0.000072/call

  vs. current full taxonomy: 2,500 tokens × $0.08/1M = $0.0002/call

  Saving: 64% per call
  At 10M calls/day: ~$1,280/day saved → ~$465K/year

  ---
  The honest phased recommendation

  Now (you have ~20-30 intents, traffic is ramping):

  Keep the current single-call architecture. It's working. But start doing two
  things:
  1. Instrument slm_classification logs broken down by intent to get the actual
  distribution — confirm the 85/15 split
  2. Partition the INTENT_REGISTRY by domain now, even if you're not using a
  cascade yet — this is free and positions you for Phase 2

  In 3-6 months (when you have actual cost data and 30+ intents):

  Implement the two-stage cascade. Stage 1 is trivial to build — it's just a
  5-way router with a 200-token prompt. Stage 2 reuses the existing taxonomy
  format, just domain-scoped.

  The load_more_tools / confidence-gated approach:

  Worth A/B testing as a middle path — it's simpler than the cascade. But gate
  it behind metrics. Specifically: measure the false positive rate (how often
  primary-intent users trigger needs_more_context). If it's above 3%, the
  latency tax makes it worse than the current system even though the cost looks
  better on paper.

  ---
  Where We Land

  ┌────────────────┬───────┬────────────┬─────────┬────────────┬──────────┐
  │                │ Cost  │            │         │            │ Longevit │
  │    Approach    │  at   │  Quality   │ Latency │ Complexity │    y     │
  │                │ scale │            │         │            │          │
  ├────────────────┼───────┼────────────┼─────────┼────────────┼──────────┤
  │ Full taxonomy  │       │            │         │            │ Poor     │
  │ (current)      │ High  │ Best       │ 1 call  │ Low        │ (grows   │
  │                │       │            │         │            │ forever) │
  ├────────────────┼───────┼────────────┼─────────┼────────────┼──────────┤
  │ Terse          │ Mediu │ Compromise │ 1 call  │ Medium     │ Medium   │
  │ secondary      │ m     │ d          │         │            │          │
  ├────────────────┼───────┼────────────┼─────────┼────────────┼──────────┤
  │                │       │ Medium     │         │            │          │
  │ load_more_tool │ Mediu │ (false     │ Variabl │ Medium     │ Medium   │
  │ s              │ m     │ positive   │ e       │            │          │
  │                │       │ risk)      │         │            │          │
  ├────────────────┼───────┼────────────┼─────────┼────────────┼──────────┤
  │ Hierarchical   │       │ Best per   │ ~1.3    │ Medium-hig │          │
  │ cascade        │ Low   │ domain     │ calls   │ h          │ Best     │
  │                │       │            │ avg     │            │          │
  └────────────────┴───────┴────────────┴─────────┴────────────┴──────────┘

  The cascade is more engineering work upfront but it's the architecture that
  doesn't become a problem later. The load_more_tools approach is a reasonable
  intermediate step if you want cost savings sooner without committing to the
  cascade yet — but instrument it carefully before shipping.

       11 +Output:  domain + confidence  Output: full SLMOutput JSON     
       12 +Latency: ≤40ms                Latency: ≤120ms                 
       13 +Node:    route_domain_node    Node: classify_node             
       14 +```                                                           
       15  
       12 -**Model:** `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 (current; Gemini Flash a
          -s benchmark candidate)`                                       
       13 -**Latency budget:** ≤ 150ms (classification only, no tool call
          -s)                                                            
       14 -**Prompt cache:** Sections 1–4 are static per registry version
          - — prime cache on cold start. Cache key includes `registry_has
          -h` (SHA256 of INTENT_REGISTRY + FILTER_REGISTRY JSON); cache i
          -s invalidated and re-primed automatically on registry change. 
       16 +**Why the cascade:**                                          
       17 +- The full INTENT_REGISTRY across all domains is ~2,500 tokens
          +. At scale (10M calls/day) this costs ~$2,000/day in cached re
          +ads.                                                          
       18 +- Domain-specific taxonomy files are ~800 tokens each — 68% ch
          +eaper for the same quality.                                   
       19 +- Domains are independently cacheable: adding a `locality` sub
          +-intent only invalidates the locality domain cache. All other 
          +domain caches stay warm.                                      
       20 +- Adding new domains or intents never bloats sibling domains. 
          +The taxonomy scales horizontally instead of vertically.       
       21  
       16 -The pipeline calls the classifier through `ClassifierPort` (se
          -e `solid-architecture.md` — Adapter Interfaces). Swapping the 
          -underlying model (Haiku → Gemini Flash) requires only a new ad
          -apter implementing this protocol — no pipeline node changes.  
       22 +**Protocol interfaces** (see `solid-architecture.md` — Adapter
          + Interfaces):                                                 
       23 +- Stage 1: `DomainRouterPort` injected into `route_domain_node
          +`                                                             
       24 +- Stage 2: `ClassifierPort` injected into `classify_node`     
       25  
       18 -> **Architecture note:** The intent taxonomy injected into thi
          -s prompt (Section 2) is generated                             
       19 -> from `INTENT_REGISTRY` at startup. The filter delta rules (S
          -ection 3) are generated from                                  
       20 -> `FILTER_REGISTRY`. Do not edit these sections directly — edi
          -t the registries.                                             
       21 -> See [solid-architecture.md](./solid-architecture.md) for the
          - full registry definitions and the                            
       22 -> `registry_hash` cache-key rule (Part 5 — Middleware Pipeline

       67 +## Stage 1 — Domain Router                                    
       68  
       44 -`classify_node` wraps the SLM call with `asyncio.wait_for(time
          -out=2.0)`. On timeout or 5xx after 2 retries (tenacity exponen
          -tial backoff, max 2 attempts), the pipeline short-circuits wit
          -h `main_intent: 'out_of_scope', sub_intent: 'out_of_scope_quer
          -y'` — serving a "I'm having trouble understanding that right n
          -ow" response rather than hanging the user. The timeout event i
          -s logged as `slm_classification_timeout` and counted toward th
          -e alert threshold.                                            
       69 +### Prompt: `prompts/slm/domain_router.md`                    
       70  
       46 -The SLM HTTP client is shared across requests via a connection
          - pool (not re-instantiated per turn).                         
       71 +This file is entirely static (never changes per-request) — it 
          +is always served from the prompt cache after the first request
          + of each 5-minute window.

       75 +Classify the user message into exactly one domain.            
       76 +                                                              
       77 +DOMAINS:

          +ies from live inventory.                                      
       79 +                       BHK, price, locality, amenity, property
          + type, listing type filters.

          +nished apartments in Bandra"                                  
       81 +                                                              
       82 +  property_detail    — information about a specific named or a
          +ctive property.                                               
       83 +                       Photos, floor plan, EMI, contact seller
          +, similar properties.                                         
       84 +                       "show me photos", "what's the EMI", "co
          +nnect with seller"                                            
       85 +                                                              
       86 +  locality           — locality or area research, trends, comm
          +ute, locality comparison.                                     
       87 +                       "what's Powai like", "compare Andheri a

      101 +  - "this property", "the third one", "it" → use PREVIOUS_DOMA

      206  ## Evaluation Framework
      207  
      190 -Maintain a ground-truth test set of ≥500 labeled examples: `(m
          -essage, session_context, expected_main_intent, expected_sub_in
          -tent)`. Run after every INTENT_REGISTRY change or prompt edit.
      208 +**Two eval suites — one per stage:**                          
      209  
      192 -**Targets:** ≥95% exact match on `main_intent`, ≥90% on `sub_i
          -ntent`.                                                       
      210 +### Stage 1 Eval (Domain Router)                              
      211  
      194 -Track per-intent recall to catch per-class regressions. A drop
          - in `locality_research` recall while overall accuracy holds of
          -ten means the new intent is cannibalizing it.                 
      212 +≥200 labeled examples: `(message, previous_domain, expected_do
          +main)`.                                                       
      213  
      214 +**Targets:** ≥98% domain accuracy (5-way classification is muc
          +h simpler than full intent).                                  
      215 +                                                              
      216 +Key test cases:                                               
      217 +- Pronoun references: "this property" → `property_detail` (not
          + `property_search`)                                           
      218 +- Cross-domain signals: "compare Andheri and Bandra prices" → 
          +`locality` (not `property_search`)                            
      219 +- Ambiguous: "show me 2bhk" alone → `property_search` at 0.95 
          +confidence                                                    
      220 +- Low-confidence: single-word "hi" → `out_of_scope`           
      221 +                                                              
      222 +Alert if domain router false-positive rate on primary intents 
          +(`property_search`) exceeds 3% — this means users are getting 
          +2 SLM calls for common queries.                               
      223 +                                                              
      224 +### Stage 2 Eval (Domain-Scoped Intent Classifier)            
      225 +                                                              
      226 +≥300 labeled examples per domain (≥1,500 total): `(message, se
          +ssion_context, domain, expected_main_intent, expected_sub_inte
          +nt, expected_filter_delta)`.                                  
      227 +                                                              
      228 +**Targets per domain:**                                       
      229 +- ≥95% exact match on `sub_intent` within the domain          
      230 +- ≥90% filter delta key accuracy (correct keys extracted)     
      231 +                                                              
      232 +Domain-scoped evals catch regressions without cross-domain noi
          +se. A drop in `locality/commute_time` recall is now visible wi
          +thout it being masked by high `property_search` volume.       
      233 +                                                              
      234 +### Alerts (10-minute rolling window, both stages)            
      235 +                                                              
      236 +| Metric | Warning | Critical |                               
      237 +|---|---|---|                                                 
      238 +| Stage 1 `domain_router_timeout` | > 0.5% | > 2% |           
      239 +| Stage 1 `out_of_scope` rate | > 5% | > 10% |                
      240 +| Stage 2 `slm_classification_timeout` | > 0.5% | > 2% |      
      241 +| Stage 2 `cross_domain_intent` rejections | > 1% | > 3% |    
      242 +| Stage 2 `clarification_needed` rate | > 10% | > 20% |       
      243 +| Stage 2 `unknown_intent` events | > 0 | — |                 
      244 +                                                              
      245  **Alert thresholds** (production monitoring, rolling 10-minute
            window):
      246  - `out_of_scope` rate > 5%: may indicate regression or prompt 
           injection campaign
      247  - `clarification_needed` rate > 10%: SLM is being too conserva
           tive

⏺ All clean. Here's everything that changed and why each decision was made:

  ---
  What was built

  route_domain_node (Stage 1) — new node between normalize and classify. A 5-way
  domain router with a ~170-token static prompt (prompts/slm/domain_router.md).
  Outputs domain + confidence. Hard-coded fast path: if confidence < 0.65,
  domain becomes out_of_scope without further debate.

  classify_node (Stage 2) — now domain-scoped. Receives state['domain'] and
  loads DOMAIN_TAXONOMY_PROMPTS[domain] — one of five ~800-token domain-specific
  files. For out_of_scope, returns a pre-built classification immediately with
  zero SLM tokens spent.

  DomainRouterPort — new Protocol adapter, separate from ClassifierPort. Both
  stages can be swapped independently. You can benchmark Gemini Flash on Stage 2
  only without touching Stage 1.

  DOMAIN_MAIN_INTENTS — cross-check dict in validate_slm_node. If Stage 2
  returns an intent that belongs to a different domain (cross-domain
  hallucination), it gets caught here and treated as out_of_scope rather than
  silently misrouted.

  domain field in BotState — set by Stage 1, read by Stage 2 and
  validate_slm_node.

  Two separate metrics events per turn — domain_routing (Stage 1) and
  slm_classification (Stage 2). This lets you measure Stage 1 accuracy, Stage 1
  false-positive rate on primary intents, and Stage 2 accuracy per domain
  independently.

  Cost outcome at 10M calls/day: ~$1,026/day vs ~$2,120/day. ~$394K/year saving.
  The out_of_scope fast path means the ~15% of unclear/safety/chitchat turns
  pay only 212 tokens instead of 2,650 — an additional 92% saving on that slice.

  OCP compliance — adding a new domain is 9 steps (documented in the checklist).
  Adding a new intent to an existing domain is 7 steps, none of which touch
  route_domain_node or any other domain's prompt.

⏺ Final quick verification:

⏺ All in order. Here's what was built and why each decision was made:

  ---
  MODEL_REGISTRY (solid-architecture.md Part 15) — the single config object that
  owns every AI model assignment. Each entry has a task_id (stable, never
  changes even when models change), a description explaining why this model was
  chosen for this task, a QualityContract (measurable thresholds that a
  challenger must meet before promotion), a CostProfile (per-token pricing +
  expected tokens per call → daily_cost() always computable from current
  config), and fallback_behavior (what happens when the model is unavailable).

  Adapter pattern — ADAPTER_REGISTRY maps adapter class names to
  implementations. Adding a new provider (Google, OpenAI, self-hosted vLLM) is:
  implement the Protocol + register in ADAPTER_REGISTRY. The graph never sees
  the provider.

  SelfHostedChatAdapter — documents the exact wire contract. Same
  OpenAI-compatible API. Cost model is explicitly noted as GPU-amortized (not
  per-token), tracked via SelfHostedMetrics separately from CostProfile.
  Self-hosted break-even math is documented: not worth it at 1M/day for a single
  domain; compelling at 3M+/day for multiple domains simultaneously or if you
  need on-premises.

  ModelRouter — integrates with the existing ACTIVE_EXPERIMENTS system. Same
  deterministic session-based hashing. Model experiments use
  ExperimentConfig(type='model_variant') — no new mechanism needed. Every log
  line already carries experiment_id and experiment_variant for SQL-level
  analysis.

  No auto-promotion — documented explicitly. Variant must meet QualityContract
  thresholds over 5K calls and 7 days, then a human approves via a
  MODEL_REGISTRY update PR. This is intentional — model regressions are hard to
  detect from aggregate metrics alone.

  Cost reality at 1M/day — $1,356/day (~$495K/year). Tier 3b (Sonnet) is 34% of
  total cost from only 7% of calls. That's the number to watch. The SLM cascade
  saves ~$171/day (~$62K/year) vs the old monolithic classifier — useful but not
  dramatic at 1M volume; it becomes significant at 10M+.

           +ation)                                                       
      5178 +    business_metrics: list[str]     # metric names to surface
           + in the experiment dashboard                                 
      5179 +                                                             
      5180 +@dataclass                                                   
      5181 +class GuardrailSpec:                                         
      5182 +    metric:       str     # metric name                      
      5183 +    max_delta:    float   # maximum allowed degradation (posi
           +tive = more is worse)                                        
      5184 +    direction:    str     # 'increase_bad' | 'decrease_bad'  
      5185 +    # Example: max_delta=0.05 direction='increase_bad' on 'er
           +ror_rate'                                                    
      5186 +    # means: variant error_rate must not exceed control error
           +_rate + 5pp                                                  
      5187 +```                                                          
      5188 +                                                             
      5189 +**Pre-defined metrics per experiment type:**

      5285 +                                                             
      5286 +### LLM Output Rubric (automated)                            
      5287 +                                                             
      5288 +The `llm_output_rubric_score` metric is computed by `validate
           +_output_node` on every Tier 3 turn. Not a human score — a rul
           +e-based rubric run after each LLM call:                      
      5289 +                                                             
      5290 +```python                                                    
      5291 +@dataclass                                                   
      5292 +class RubricDimension:                                       
      5293 +    name:   str                                              
      5294 +    weight: float   # weights sum to 1.0                     
      5295 +    check:  Callable[[str, BotState], float]   # returns 0.0–
           +1.0                                                          
      5296 +                                                             
      5297 +LLM_OUTPUT_RUBRIC: list[RubricDimension] = [                 
      5298 +    RubricDimension('no_validation_violations', 0.30,        
      5299 +        lambda text, state: 0.0 if validate_bot_output(text, 
           +current_intent(state)).violations else 1.0                   
      5300 +    ),                                                       
      5301 +    RubricDimension('length_appropriate',        0.20,       
      5302 +        lambda text, state: _length_score(text, state)   # 1.
           +0 if 1-3 sentences for followup                              
      5303 +    ),                                                       
      5304 +    RubricDimension('no_phase1_repeat',          0.20,       
      5305 +        lambda text, state: 0.0 if state.get('summary_emitted
           +') and _starts_with_summary(text) else 1.0                   
      5306 +    ),                                                       
      5307 +    RubricDimension('factual_grounding',         0.20,       
      5308 +        lambda text, state: _grounding_score(text, state['pre
           +_fetched_data'])                                             
      5309 +        # checks that any price/area/location claim appears i
           +n pre_fetched_data                                           
      5310 +    ),                                                       
      5311 +    RubricDimension('language_match',            0.10,       
      5312 +        lambda text, state: _language_match(text, state['norm
           +alized_message'])                                            
      5313 +        # response language matches user message language (ba
           +sic Hindi detection)                                         
      5314 +    ),                                                       
      5315 +]                                                            
      5316 +                                                             
      5317 +def compute_rubric_score(text: str, state: BotState) -> float
           +:                                                            
      5318 +    return sum(d.weight * d.check(text, state) for d in LLM_O
           +UTPUT_RUBRIC)                                                
      5319 +```                                                          
      5320 +                                                             
      5321 +The rubric score is emitted in every `llm_call` log event. Da
           +shboard shows rolling 7-day p25/p50/p75. Alert if p50 drops b
           +elow 0.70.                                                   
      5322 +                                                             
      5323 +### Graduation Procedure (updated)                           
      5324 +                                                             
      5325 +An experiment graduates when ALL gates pass:                 
      5326 +                                                             
      5327 +| Gate | Requirement |                                       
      5328  |---|---|
      5161 -| Statistical significance | p < 0.05 on primary metric |    
      5162 -| Eval set quality | ≥ `passing_threshold` from prompt block 
           -frontmatter |                                                
      5163 -| Regression guard | Latency, error rate, and cost within ±5%
           - of control |                                                
      5164 -| Minimum sample | ≥ 500 turns per variant |                 
      5329 +| Primary KPI | Statistically significant improvement or non-
           +inferiority at `confidence_level` |                          
      5330 +| Sample size | ≥ `min_sample_per_variant` calls AND ≥ `min_o
           +bservation_days` elapsed |                                   
      5331 +| All guardrails | No guardrail exceeded in either direction 
           +|                                                            
      5332 +| Human sign-off | Required for `model_variant` and `flow_var
           +iant`; optional for `prompt_variant` |                       
      5333  
      5166 -Graduation procedure:                                        
      5167 -1. Commit the winning variant as the new default in the promp
           -t block or INTENT_REGISTRY                                   
      5168 -2. Version-bump the changed block (patch/minor/major per Part
           - 7 policy)                                                   
      5169 -3. Set `enabled: false` and `end_date` on the ExperimentConfi
           -g                                                            
      5170 -4. Deploy — the old variant is never served again            
      5334 +Graduation steps:                                            
      5335 +1. Merge PR that updates MODEL_REGISTRY (for `model_variant`)
           + or prompt block / INTENT_REGISTRY (for others)              
      5336 +2. Version-bump changed artifacts per Part 7 policy          
      5337 +3. Set `enabled: false` + `end_date` on ExperimentConfig in `
           +experiments.yaml`                                            
      5338 +4. Delete variant fixtures from `tests/fixtures/` that are no
           +w the new control                                            
      5339  
      5172 -**Rollback:** set `enabled: false` immediately; traffic rever
           -ts to the unmodified code path                               
      5340 +**Abort criteria:** abort immediately (without waiting for sa
           +mple size) if any guardrail exceeds 3× its `max_delta` thresh
           +old. Set `enabled: false`, page on-call.                     
      5341  within one hot-reload cycle (≤60s). No deploy needed for roll
            back.

      5678 +### Calibrated Model Evaluation                              
      5679 +                                                             
      5680 +The model eval harness differs from the prompt eval harness i
           +n a critical way: it does **calibrated comparison**, not exac
           +t-match assertion. Model outputs are evaluated on a multi-dim
           +ensional rubric so that equivalent outputs that differ in phr
           +asing don't fail the test.                                   
      5681 +                                                             
      5682 +#### Case file format (`tests/model_eval/<task_id>/cases.json
           +l`)                                                          
      5683 +                                                             
      5684 +```json                                                      
      5685 +{"id":"case_001","input":{"message":"show me 2bhk in powai","
           +history":[],"active_filters":{},"previous_intent":null,"previ
           +ous_domain":null},"expected":{"domain":"property_search","con
           +fidence_min":0.90},"calibration":{"strict_fields":["domain"],
           +"soft_fields":[],"disqualifiers":[{"field":"domain","value":"
           +out_of_scope"}]},"tags":["primary","hindi_ok"],"notes":"Basic
           + property search — must route to property_search"}           
      5686 +{"id":"case_002","input":{"message":"tell me about lodha pala
           +va","history":[],"active_filters":{},"previous_intent":null,"
           +previous_domain":null},"expected":{"domain":"project_research
           +","confidence_min":0.80},"calibration":{"strict_fields":["dom
           +ain"],"soft_fields":[],"disqualifiers":[{"field":"domain","va
           +lue":"property_search"}]},"tags":["primary"],"notes":"Named p
           +roject query — must not route to property_search"}           
      5687 +{"id":"case_003","input":{"message":"doosri aur teesri locali
           +ties pasand hai","history":[{"user":"show me localities simil
           +ar to powai","domain":"locality"}],"active_filters":{},"previ
           +ous_intent":"trending_localities","previous_domain":"locality
           +"},"expected":{"domain":"property_search"},"calibration":{"st
           +rict_fields":["domain"],"soft_fields":[],"disqualifiers":[]},
           +"tags":["hindi","ordinal"],"notes":"Hindi ordinal reference a
           +fter locality carousel — should pivot to property_search"}   
      5688 +```                                                          
      5689 +                                                             
      5690 +For Stage 2 (intent classifier) cases:                       
      5691 +```json                                                      
      5692 +{"id":"case_ps_001","input":{"message":"2bhk flat in andheri 
           +under 80 lakhs","history":[],"active_filters":{},"previous_in
           +tent":null},"expected":{"main_intent":"property_search","sub_
           +intent":"filter_search","filter_delta":{"bhk":[2],"localities
           +":["Andheri"],"price_max":8000000}},"calibration":{"strict_fi
           +elds":["main_intent","sub_intent"],"soft_fields":[{"field":"f
           +ilter_delta.bhk","compare":"exact"},{"field":"filter_delta.pr
           +ice_max","compare":"within_10pct"},{"field":"filter_delta.loc
           +alities","compare":"entity_match"}],"disqualifiers":[{"field"
           +:"clarification_needed","condition":"not_null"}]},"tags":["pr
           +imary","hindi_units"],"notes":"'80 lakhs' = 8000000. Price wi
           +thin 10% acceptable — unit conversion is approximate."}      
      5693 +```                                                          
      5694 +                                                             
      5695 +#### Calibrated comparison logic                             
      5696 +                                                             
      5697 +```python                                                    
      5698 +@dataclass                                                   
      5699 +class SoftField:                                             
      5700 +    field:   str    # dot-notation path into output dict     
      5701 +    compare: Literal['exact', 'within_10pct', 'entity_match',
           + 'subset', 'key_presence']                                   
      5702 +    # exact:         field value == expected value exactly   
      5703 +    # within_10pct:  abs(actual - expected) / expected <= 0.1
           +0                                                            
      5704 +    # entity_match:  actual entity name is a substring of exp
           +ected or vice versa                                          
      5705 +    #                ("Andheri West" matches "Andheri"; "andh
           +eri" matches "Andheri West")                                 
      5706 +    # subset:        every element of expected appears in act
           +ual (list fields, e.g. bhk)                                  
      5707 +    # key_presence:  filter_delta contains at least the expec
           +ted keys (values not checked)                                
      5708 +                                                             
      5709 +def evaluate_case(actual: dict, expected: dict, calibration: 
           +CaseCalibration) -> CaseResult:                              
      5710 +    failures = []                                            
      5711 +                                                             
      5712 +    # Strict fields — exact match required                   
      5713 +    for field in calibration.strict_fields:                  
      5714 +        act = get_nested(actual, field)                      
      5715 +        exp = get_nested(expected, field)                    
      5716 +        if act != exp:                                       
      5717 +            failures.append(f'STRICT {field}: got {act!r}, ex
           +pected {exp!r}')                                             
      5718 +                                                             
      5719 +    # Soft fields — calibrated comparison                    
      5720 +    for soft in calibration.soft_fields:                     
      5721 +        act = get_nested(actual, soft.field)                 
      5722 +        exp = get_nested(expected, soft.field)               
      5723 +        if not _soft_compare(act, exp, soft.compare):        
      5724 +            failures.append(f'SOFT {soft.field} ({soft.compar
           +e}): got {act!r}, expected {exp!r}')                         
      5725 +                                                             
      5726 +    # Disqualifiers — automatic fail regardless of other resu
           +lts                                                          
      5727 +    for disq in calibration.disqualifiers:                   
      5728 +        act = get_nested(actual, disq.field)                 
      5729 +        if _disqualifier_triggered(act, disq):               
      5730 +            failures.append(f'DISQUALIFIER: {disq.field} = {a
           +ct!r} (forbidden)')                                          
      5731 +                                                             
      5732 +    passed = len(failures) == 0                              
      5733 +    return CaseResult(case_id=case.id, passed=passed, failure
           +s=failures)                                                  
      5734 +```                                                          
      5735 +

      5757 +                                                             
      5758 +#### Model eval runner                                       
      5759 +                                                             
      5760 +```python                                                    
      5761 +# tests/model_eval/runner.py                                 
      5762 +                                                             
      5763 +class ModelEvalRunner:                                       
      5764 +    """Runs calibrated eval cases against any ModelAssignment
           + (control or variant)."""                                    
      5765 +                                                             
      5766 +    def __init__(self, task_id: str, assignment: ModelAssignm
           +ent, cases_file: Path):                                      
      5767 +        self.task_id    = task_id                            
      5768 +        self.assignment = assignment                         
      5769 +        self.adapter    = build_adapter(assignment)          
      5770 +        self.cases      = [CaseFile(**json.loads(l)) for l in
           + cases_file.read_text().splitlines()]                        
      5771 +                                                             
      5772 +    async def run(self) -> EvalReport:                       
      5773 +        results = await asyncio.gather(*[self._eval_case(c) f
           +or c in self.cases])                                         
      5774 +        passed  = sum(1 for r in results if r.passed)        
      5775 +        report  = EvalReport(                                
      5776 +            task_id        = self.task_id,                   
      5777 +            model_id       = self.assignment.model_id,       
      5778 +            provider       = self.assignment.provider,       
      5779 +            total          = len(results),                   
      5780 +            passed         = passed,                         
      5781 +            accuracy       = passed / len(results),          
      5782 +            failures       = [r for r in results if not r.pas
           +sed],                                                        
      5783 +            latency_p95_ms = int(sorted(r.latency_ms for r in
           + results)[int(len(results)*0.95)]),                          
      5784 +        )                                                    
      5785 +        contract = self.assignment.quality_contract          
      5786 +        report.meets_contract = (                            
      5787 +            (contract.min_accuracy is None or report.accuracy
           + >= contract.min_accuracy) and                               
      5788 +            (contract.p95_latency_ms is None or report.latenc
           +y_p95_ms <= contract.p95_latency_ms)                         
      5789 +        )                                                    
      5790 +        return report                                        
      5791 +                                                             
      5792 +    async def _eval_case(self, case: CaseFile) -> CaseResult:
      5793 +        start  = time.monotonic()                            
      5794 +        actual = await self.adapter.classify(case.input)    #
           + or .route() for domain_router                               
      5795 +        ms     = int((time.monotonic() - start) * 1000)      
      5796 +        result = evaluate_case(actual, case.expected, case.ca
           +libration)                                                   
      5797 +        result.latency_ms = ms                               
      5798 +        return result                                        
      5799 +```

      6287 +### Model Selection Guides                                   
      6288 +                                                             
      6289 +Each task entry in MODEL_REGISTRY carries a `description` fie
           +ld. The extended guide below documents the reasoning behind c
           +urrent assignments and the criteria for evaluating replacemen
           +ts. **Read this before proposing a model change.**           
      6290 +                                                             
      6291 +```python                                                    
      6292 +@dataclass                                                   
      6293 +class ModelSelectionGuide:                                   
      6294 +    task_id:            str                                  
      6295 +    why_ai_not_rules:   str    # Why can't this be rule-based
           +? What requires a model?                                     
      6296 +    input_profile:      str    # What does the input look lik
           +e? Size, language, variability.                              
      6297 +    output_contract:    str    # What must the output ALWAYS

      6298 +    failure_modes:      list[str]  # How can this model fail,

      6299 +    selection_priority: str    # 'accuracy_first' | 'cost_fir
           +st' | 'latency_first'                                        
      6300 +    disqualifiers:      list[str]  # Hard limits. A model fai
           +ls these → eliminated immediately.                           
      6301 +    eval_case_file:     str    # Path to calibrated test case
           +s for this task.

           + and rejected, with reason.

⏺ 61 distinct references across the new additions. Here's what was built and the
  reasoning behind each decision:

  ---
  What was added and why

  ExperimentMetrics (Part 13 extension)

  Every ExperimentConfig now must declare metrics before going live — enforced
  at startup. Previously, graduation criteria were vague ("p < 0.05 on primary
  metric" without defining which metric). Now each experiment type has:

  - primary_kpi — the one number the experiment is trying to move. For model
  swaps: sub_intent_accuracy (classifiers) or llm_output_rubric_score (LLM). For
  prompt variants: task-specific. For flow variants: fetch_latency_p50_ms.
  Forces the team to agree on what "better" means before the experiment starts,
  not after.
  - guardrails — what must NOT regress. Latency, error rate, cross-domain
  hallucination rate, output validation violations. A variant that wins on
  accuracy but adds 200ms of latency is rejected automatically.
  - business_metrics — downstream proxies (session continuation rate, contact
  seller rate, properties viewed). Not gating, but surfaced in the dashboard.
  These catch quality regressions that the rubric misses.
  - Abort criteria — if any guardrail exceeds 3× its threshold, kill the
  experiment immediately without waiting for sample size. Prevents runaway
  degradation.

  LLM_OUTPUT_RUBRIC (Part 13)

  Automated, rubric-based quality score computed on every Tier 3 turn. Five
  dimensions: validation violations (30%), response length (20%), phase-1
  non-repeat (20%), factual grounding (20%), language match (10%). Emitted in
  every llm_call log. This turns LLM quality from a subjective human judgment
  into a measurable metric that dashboards can track and experiments can gate
  on.

  Test taxonomy (Part 14 extension)

  Four distinct test layers with clear separation:

  - unit/ — pure Python, no I/O, sub-5s. Every node tested in isolation with
  make_base_state. Already existed partially; now has required coverage for all
  nodes including route_domain_node.
  - prompt/ — structural validation with no API calls. Required sections per
  prompt file, token budget enforcement, cross-registry consistency (every
  template intent must have a SUMMARY_BUILDERS entry). Catches the class of bug
  where someone adds an intent to the registry but forgets to update
  FOLLOWUP_PROMPT_BLOCKS.
  - model_eval/ — calibrated accuracy tests, runnable against any adapter. Mock
  mode for CI (fast, free), real-model mode before deploys. Minimum case counts
  enforced at startup.
  - integration/ — full graph with mock external APIs, asserts on SSE event
  sequence. build_test_graph() utility makes every adapter overrideable so you
  can test any combination.

  Calibrated model evaluation (Part 14)

  The key insight: model outputs are not binary. evaluate_case uses three
  comparison modes:
  - strict_fields — exact match (domain, main_intent, sub_intent). A model that
  says property_research instead of project_research fails hard.
  - soft_fields — calibrated (price within 10%, entity name substring match, BHK
  subset match). A model that says price_max: 7900000 when the expected is
  8000000 (80L) passes — unit conversion is inherently approximate.
  - disqualifiers — automatic fail conditions regardless of other results.
  clarification_needed != null for a case that should be classified directly is
  a disqualifier.

  This prevents test flakiness from natural output variation while still
  catching genuine regressions.

  ModelSelectionGuide (Part 15)

  Four detailed guides for domain_router, property_search classifier,
  llm_tier3a, llm_tier3b. Each documents: why AI (not rules) is needed, what the
  input profile looks like, what the output must always contain, the failure
  modes and their user impact, the selection priority, hard disqualifiers, and
  models explicitly tested and rejected with reasons. The not_suitable list is
  especially important — it records institutional memory about what was tried
  and why it failed, preventing the team from re-evaluating the same models
  repeatedly.

        69 -## Part 1 — INTENT_REGISTRY                                  
        70 -                                                             
        71 -### Python Schema                                            
        72 -                                                             
        73 -```python                                                    
        74 -from pydantic import BaseModel                               
        75 -from typing import Literal, Optional                         
        76 -                                                             
        77 -Tier = Literal[0, 1, 2, '3a', '3b']                          
        78 -ModelHint = Literal['haiku', 'sonnet'] | None                
        79 -ParamSource = Literal['session', 'entity_resolution', 'filter
           -_delta']                                                     
        80 -                                                             
        81 -# Stage 1 domain routing output. Determines which domain-scop
           -ed taxonomy                                                  
        82 -# is loaded for Stage 2 classification.                      
        83 -DomainType = Literal[                                        
        84 -    'property_search',   # browsing inventory, filter changes
           -, search alerts                                              
        85 -    'property_detail',   # specific property: gallery, floor 
           -plan, EMI, contact, similar                                  
        86 -    'locality',          # locality research, trends, commute
           -, comparison                                                 
        87 -    'project_research',  # new-launch projects and builders  
        88 -    'portfolio',         # personal activity: saved, viewed, 
           -recent searches, recommendations                             
        89 -    'out_of_scope',      # chitchat, safety, gibberish — Stag
           -e 2 skipped                                                  
        90 -]                                                            
        91 -                                                             
        92 -class DataRequirement(BaseModel):                            
        93 -    """Declares what the orchestrator must fetch BEFORE the L
           -LM call.                                                     
        94 -    All items in the same parallel_group are fetched concurre
           -ntly (asyncio.gather).                                       
        95 -    Groups are ordered: group 1 runs first, group 2 runs afte
           -r group 1 completes, etc.                                    
        96 -    entity_index: for entity_resolution sources, which resolv
           -ed entity to use (0 = first, 1 = second).                    
        97 -    """                                                      
        98 -    tool:           str                                      
        99 -    params_source:  ParamSource                              
       100 -    entity_index:   Optional[int] = None   # entity_resolutio
           -n only; None = first (index 0)                               
       101 -    parallel_group: int                                      
       102 -    # Per-fetch timeout override. If omitted, TOOL_DEFAULT_TI
           -MEOUTS[tool] is used.                                        
       103 -    # Group-level: the group completes when all settled (retu
           -rn_exceptions=True), not all resolved.                       
       104 -    timeout_ms:     Optional[int] = None                     
       105 -    # Storage key in state['pre_fetched_data']. Defaults to t
           -ool name if omitted.                                         
       106 -    # REQUIRED when the same tool appears more than once in d
           -ata_requirements                                             
       107 -    # (e.g., comparison intents calling getDemandSupplyInsigh
           -t for two entities).                                         
       108 -    # Without a unique key, the second result overwrites the 
           -first.                                                       
       109 -    # Convention: '<tool>:<entity_index>'  →  'getDemandSuppl
           -yInsight:0'                                                  
       110 -    fetch_key:      Optional[str] = None                     
       111 -                                                             
       112 -class IntentRecord(BaseModel):                               
       113 -    # Identity                                               
       114 -    main_intent: str                                         
       115 -    sub_intent:  str                                         
       116 -                                                             
       117 -    # Routing                                                
       118 -    tier:  Tier                                              
       119 -    model: ModelHint          # None for tiers 0–2 (no LLM ca
           -ll)                                                          
       120 -                                                             
       121 -    # What the orchestrator pre-fetches before the LLM turn. 
       122 -    # fetch_data node executes these in parallel groups.     
       123 -    # For Tier 0/1/2: empty [] (no LLM call) or the computati
           -on the orchestrator runs.                                    
       124 -    data_requirements: list[DataRequirement]                 
       125 -                                                             
       126 -    # Tools the LLM MAY call as a fallback if pre-fetched dat
           -a is insufficient.                                           
       127 -    # For most intents: [] — the LLM has NO tools and just fo
           -rmats pre-fetched data.                                      
       128 -    # For a small set: one safety-net tool for same-turn foll
           -ow-up questions.                                             
       129 -    residual_tools: list[str]                                
       130 -                                                             
       131 -    # Session state keys injected into the LLM system prompt 
           -for this intent.                                             
       132 -    session_inject: list[str]                                
       133 -                                                             
       134 -    # Filter keys to PRESERVE when pivoting TO this intent fr
           -om another                                                   
       135 -    carry_over_keys: list[str]                               
       136 -                                                             
       137 -    # Filter keys to CLEAR when pivoting TO this intent from 
           -another                                                      
       138 -    clear_keys: list[str]                                    
       139 -                                                             
       140 -    # Whether orchestrator should pre-resolve entities_mentio
           -ned before LLM call                                          
       141 -    pre_resolve_entities: bool                               
       142 -                                                             
       143 -    # Whether auth token must be present before routing here 
       144 -    requires_auth: bool                                      
       145 -                                                             
       146 -    # Description used in taxonomy template injected into pro
           -mpts                                                         
       147 -    description: str                                         
       148 -```

      2261 -### Template Rendering Rules                                 
      2262 -                                                             
      2263 -1. **Template blocks are pre-rendered at startup** from the r
           -egistry, not on every request. The rendered string is the sta
           -tic input to the prompt cache.                               
      2264 -2. **Registry changes require re-render + cache invalidation.
           -** Add `registry_hash` to cache key — a SHA256 of the registr
           -y JSON triggers re-render when either registry changes.      
      2265 -3. **Examples are appended after the corresponding block** th
           -ey illustrate. They are part of the same cached section.     
      2266 -4. **`07-session-context.md.tmpl` is never cached** — it chan
           -ges every request. It is the only dynamic section.
